query: How can we reduce incident resolution time?

per_column.name: resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: This is the outcome itself (resolution_time expressed in hours), not a treatment or confounder.

per_column.name: assignee_avg_resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: Assignee skill/speed proxy is a common cause: it influences how quickly incidents are resolved and can correlate with which cases get assigned to whom. Not named in the query. However it borders on being a proxy for assignment lever rather than a clean adjustment variable.

per_column.name: category_avg_resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: Category difficulty is a common cause affecting resolution time and correlating with treatments like assignment/handoff. Category exists in the original table but its difficulty summary is not named in the analytical query text.

per_column.name: resolution_vs_assignee_avg
per_column.rationale: A residual computed from the outcome minus the assignee average; it is a transformation of the outcome, not a pre-treatment confounder.

per_column.name: priority_urgency_score
per_column.rationale: Priority/urgency is a common cause of both handling/assignment decisions and resolution time. Priority is present in the original table and clearly implied as relevant context, though it could also be viewed as an intervenable lever (triage assignment).

per_column.name: no_handoff
per_column.rationale: Whether an incident was handled without reassignment/handoff is an intervenable operational lever an actor can set (routing/assignment policy), plausibly affecting resolution time.

judge.rationale: One genuinely intervenable treatment is present: no_handoff represents a settable routing/assignment policy that could reduce resolution time, satisfying claim (a). For claim (b), there are plausible confounders. category difficulty and assignee-average speed are common causes of both handoff/assignment and resolution time and are NOT named in the query, demonstrating some capability. priority_urgency is a valid confounder but is essentially named in the query context (priority column). However, the set is weakened by two of the six columns being outcome transformations (resolution_hours, resolution_vs_assignee_avg) rather than adjustment variables, and by the confounders being coarse aggregate proxies that partly overlap with the treatment mechanism (assignment). No confounder is adjusted for temporal/pre-treatment status explicitly. Overall the interventional framing is only partially realised.
